title: What design patterns are
idea: A design pattern is a named, proven solution shape for a problem that keeps coming back in object-oriented code.
points: The Gang of Four book named 23 classic patterns in three families.
Creational patterns control how objects are made.
Structural patterns control how objects are wired together.
Behavioural patterns control how objects split up work and talk.

code.title: Before: one growing function
code.caption: Every new channel adds a branch here. Try adding `push` and notice you must edit working code.

code.title: After: Strategy pattern
code.caption: Each channel is a class with `send()`. Add a `PushSender` class without touching `Notifier`.

walk.text: Two interchangeable strategies share one method name: `send(to, msg)`.
`Notifier` holds a sender in `#sender` and never checks which kind it is.
It delegates the varying part to the strategy.
The caller picks the strategy; `Notifier` stays closed for modification.

pitfalls: Do not add a pattern before the problem it solves actually shows up.
Learn the problem each pattern solves, not only its class diagram.
In JavaScript a plain function can replace a small pattern; prefer the simpler shape.

quiz.why: `print` asks whatever strategy `this.f` holds at call time. It was swapped to `Upper` before the call.

takeaway: A pattern is a named fix for a recurring design problem.

starters: How do I know which pattern fits a problem in an interview?
